1	# Developer Workforce & Compensation Trends — 2024 Stack Overflow Survey
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work
     5	
     6	## Employment Status
     7	
     8	84% of the 65,437 respondents are currently working (full-time, part-time, or freelancing). Full-time employment is the dominant mode at 69%, followed by independent contracting/freelancing at 16.4% and full-time students at 13.2%.
     9	
    10	In the United States specifically, full-time employment dropped from 69% in 2023 to 64.8% in 2024. In the U.K. and Ukraine, non-full-time respondents lean toward independent contracting, while in Germany and India they are more likely to be full-time students.
    11	
    12	## Work Environment Trends
    13	
    14	Hybrid work remains the most common arrangement at 42%, consistent with 2023. Remote work accounts for 38%. In-person work has risen for the third consecutive year — from 15% in 2022 to 16% in 2023 to 20% in 2024 — signaling a gradual return-to-office trend.
    15	
    16	## Company Size
    17	
    18	47% of respondents work for organizations with fewer than 100 employees. The distribution across 42,827 respondents:
    19	
    20	| Company Size | Share |
    21	|---|---|
    22	| Freelancer / solo | 6.1% |
    23	| 2–9 employees | 10.4% |
    24	| 10–19 employees | 8.9% |
    25	| 20–99 employees | 21.2% |
    26	| 100–499 employees | 18.5% |
    27	| 500–999 employees | 6.7% |
    28	| 1,000–4,999 employees | 11.0% |
    29	| 5,000–9,999 employees | 3.8% |
    30	| 10,000+ employees | 11.4% |
    31	
    32	## Salary by Developer Type
    33	
    34	Median annual compensation (USD, all respondents) varies dramatically by role. The top and bottom roles are shown below (22,677 salary responses, 34.7% response rate):
    35	
    36	| Developer Type | Median Salary (USD) | Avg. Years Experience |
    37	|---|---|---|
    38	| Senior Executive | $127,388 | ~17 |
    39	| Dev Advocate | $124,203 | ~16 |
    40	| Manager | $115,999 | ~15 |
    41	| Dev Experience | $109,483 | ~12 |
    42	| SRE | $99,099 | ~10 |
    43	| Cloud Infra. Engineer | $96,666 | ~13 |
    44	| Blockchain | $85,925 | ~9 |
    45	| Product Manager | $80,000 | ~14 |
    46	| Full-stack | $63,333 | ~10 |
    47	| Front-end | $48,787 | ~8 |
    48	| Student | $15,466 | ~2 |
    49	
    50	Site reliability engineers and cloud infrastructure engineers are the highest-paid purely technical roles, reflecting their critical importance in keeping digital services running. Regionally, mobile developers earn more in the U.S., data engineers top the charts in Germany and Ukraine, and back-end developers lead in India and the U.K.
    51	
    52	![Salary by developer type — bar chart](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    53	
    54	![Salary vs. experience by developer type — scatter plot](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    55	
    56	## Salary by Programming Language
    57	
    58	Developers using niche functional languages earn the most. The overall reported salary range has dropped roughly $10K compared to 2023, now averaging $60–75K USD vs. $70–85K USD last year.
    59	
    60	| Language | Median Salary (USD) | Avg. Years Experience |
    61	|---|---|---|
    62	| Erlang | ~$97,000 | ~12 |
    63	| Clojure | ~$95,000 | ~11 |
    64	| Elixir | ~$93,000 | ~11 |
    65	| Perl | ~$90,000 | ~19 |
    66	| Ruby | ~$89,000 | ~11 |
    67	| Scala | ~$88,000 | ~9 |
    68	| Go | ~$76,000 | ~9 |
    69	| Python | ~$67,000 | ~9 |
    70	| JavaScript | ~$64,000 | ~10 |
    71	| PHP | ~$49,000 | ~10 |
    72	| Dart | ~$44,000 | ~8 |
    73	| Prolog | ~$43,000 | ~9 |
    74	
    75	![Salary vs. experience by language — scatter plot](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    76	
    77	## Technology Purchasing Influence
    78	
    79	62% of respondents have influence over technology purchases at their organizations. Senior executives (99%), engineering managers (87%), and product managers (77%) wield the most influence. 60% of respondents prefer a build-and-buy approach over purely building or buying. Starting a free trial (75%) and asking other developers (73%) are the top methods for evaluating new tools.
    80	
    81	## Key Findings
    82	
    83	- **Full-time employment is softening**: U.S. full-time employment fell 4 percentage points year-over-year; freelancing and contracting remain significant at 16%+.
    84	- **In-person work is creeping back**: now at 20%, up from 15% in 2022, though hybrid (42%) still dominates.
    85	- **DevRel and leadership roles command premium pay**: Senior Executives ($127K), Dev Advocates ($124K), and Managers ($116K) top the salary chart, all with 15+ years average experience.
    86	- **Niche functional languages correlate with higher pay**: Erlang, Clojure, and Elixir developers earn >$93K median, while mainstream languages like JavaScript and PHP sit well below $65K.
    87	- **Developers are key purchase influencers**: with 62% having a say in tech buying decisions, vendor strategies should target individual contributors, not just management.

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18, bold=False,
                color=RgbColor(0x33, 0x33, 0x33), align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri", italic=False):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.runs[0]
    run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    run.font.name = font_name
    return tf


def add_bullet_text(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets, font_size=16,
                    color=RgbColor(0x33, 0x33, 0x33), font_name="Calibri",
                    bullet_color=RgbColor(0x00, 0x4D, 0x80)):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = bullet
        p.level = 0
        p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
        # bullet color via run
        if p.runs:
            p.runs[0].font.color.rgb = color
    return tf


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Theme constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)
MARGIN = Inches(0.6)

DARK_BLUE = RgbColor(0x00, 0x2B, 0x4C)      # title / header
ACCENT_BLUE = RgbColor(0x00, 0x7A, 0xCC)    # accents
LIGHT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xF5, 0xF5, 0xF5)     # background boxes
TEXT_DARK = RgbColor(0x33, 0x33, 0x33)
WHITE = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create presentation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH
prs.slide_height = SLIDE_HEIGHT

blank_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide 1: Title
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
# subtle top bar
shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.15))
shape.fill.solid()
shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_BLUE
shape.line.fill.background()

# Title
add_textbox(slide, MARGIN, Inches(2.4), SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2, Inches(1.2),
            "Developer Workforce & Compensation Trends",
            font_size=40, bold=True, color=DARK_BLUE, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
# Subtitle
add_textbox(slide, MARGIN, Inches(3.5), SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2, Inches(0.6),
            "2024 Stack Overflow Survey",
            font_size=28, bold=False, color=ACCENT_BLUE, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
# Meta
add_textbox(slide, MARGIN, Inches(4.3), SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2, Inches(0.5),
            "65,437 respondents across 180+ countries",
            font_size=20, bold=False, color=TEXT_DARK, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
# Source
add_textbox(slide, MARGIN, Inches(5.0), SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2, Inches(0.4),
            "Source: survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work",
            font_size=14, italic=True, color=RgbColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88), align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide 2: Employment Status Overview
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
# Header bar
shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(1.0))
shape.fill.solid()
shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BLUE
shape.line.fill.background()
add_textbox(slide, MARGIN, Inches(0.25), SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2, Inches(0.6),
            "84% of Developers Are Working, but Full-Time Employment Dips in the U.S.",
            font_size=26, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Body text
body_left = MARGIN
body_top = Inches(1.25)
body_w = SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2
body_h = Inches(5.5)

tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(body_left, body_top, body_w, body_h).text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True

paragraphs = [
    ("Global Employment Breakdown", True, 20),
    ("• 84% of the 65,437 respondents are currently working (full-time, part-time, or freelancing).", False, 16),
    ("• Full-time employment dominates at 69%.", False, 16),
    ("• Independent contracting / freelancing: 16.4%.", False, 16),
    ("• Full-time students: 13.2%.", False, 16),
    ("", False, 12),
    ("U.S. Shift", True, 20),
    ("• U.S. full-time employment dropped from 69% in 2023 to 64.8% in 2024.", False, 16),
    ("• Freelancing and contracting remain significant at 16%+.", False, 16),
    ("", False, 12),
    ("Regional Nuances", True, 20),
    ("• In the U.K. and Ukraine, non-full-time respondents lean toward independent contracting.", False, 16),
    ("• In Germany and India, they are more likely to be full-time students.", False, 16),
]

for i, (text, bold, size) in enumerate(paragraphs):
    if i == 0:
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    else:
        p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_DARK
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    p.space_after = Pt(6 if size == 16 else 14)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide 3: Work Environment Shift
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(1.0))
shape.fill.solid()
shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BLUE
shape.line.fill.background()
add_textbox(slide, MARGIN, Inches(0.25), SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2, Inches(0.6),
            "In-Person Work Rises to 20% While Hybrid Holds Steady at 42%",
            font_size=26, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(MARGIN, Inches(1.25), SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2, Inches(5.5)).text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True

env_paras = [
    ("Work Arrangement Trends (2022–2024)", True, 20),
    ("• Hybrid work remains the most common arrangement at 42%, consistent with 2023.", False, 16),
    ("• Remote work accounts for 38%.", False, 16),
    ("• In-person work has risen for the third consecutive year:", False, 16),
    ("   – 15% in 2022", False, 16),
    ("   – 16% in 2023", False, 16),
    ("   – 20% in 2024", False, 16),
    ("", False, 12),
    ("Implication", True, 20),
    ("• A gradual return-to-office trend is underway, though hybrid still dominates.", False, 16),
    ("• Engineering leaders should plan for flexible policies that retain talent while accommodating RTO pressure.", False, 16),
]

for i, (text, bold, size) in enumerate(env_paras):
    if i == 0:
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    else:
        p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_DARK
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    p.space_after = Pt(6 if size == 16 else 14)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide 4: Salary by Developer Type (horizontal bar chart)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(1.0))
shape.fill.solid()
shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BLUE
shape.line.fill.background()
add_textbox(slide, MARGIN, Inches(0.25), SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2, Inches(0.6),
            "Senior Executives and Dev Advocates Top $124K+ Median Salary",
            font_size=26, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Chart data (top 10 from source)
roles = [
    ("Senior Executive", 127388),
    ("Dev Advocate", 124203),
    ("Manager", 115999),
    ("Dev Experience", 109483),
    ("SRE", 99099),
    ("Cloud Infra. Engineer", 96666),
    ("Blockchain", 85925),
    ("Product Manager", 80000),
    ("Full-stack", 63333),
    ("Front-end", 48787),
]

chart_left = MARGIN
chart_top = Inches(1.2)
chart_w = SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2
chart_h = Inches(5.5)

# Draw simple horizontal bars using shapes
max_salary = max(v for _, v in roles)
bar_height = Inches(0.38)
gap = Inches(0.08)
label_w = Inches(2.4)
bar_max_w = chart_w - label_w - Inches(1.0)

for idx, (role, salary) in enumerate(roles):
    y = chart_top + idx * (bar_height + gap)
    # label
    add_textbox(slide, chart_left, y, label_w, bar_height, role,
                font_size=13, bold=False, color=TEXT_DARK, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)
    # bar
    bar_w = bar_max_w * (salary / max_salary)
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, chart_left + label_w + Inches(0.1), y + Inches(0.04), bar_w, bar_height - Inches(0.08))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_BLUE
    bar.line.fill.background()
    # value label
    add_textbox(slide, chart_left + label_w + Inches(0.1) + bar_w + Inches(0.08), y + Inches(0.02), Inches(1.2), bar_height,
                f"${salary:,}", font_size=12, bold=True, color=TEXT_DARK, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Caption
add_textbox(slide, MARGIN, Inches(6.85), SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2, Inches(0.4),
            "Source: 2024 Stack Overflow Survey (22,677 salary responses, 34.7% response rate). Reference: figure_1.jpg",
            font_size=11, italic=True, color=RgbColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88), align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide 5: Experience vs. Salary (scatter plot)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(1.0))
shape.fill.solid()
shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BLUE
shape.line.fill.background()
add_textbox(slide, MARGIN, Inches(0.25), SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2, Inches(0.6),
            "Experience Pays: Top Roles Combine 14+ Years with Six-Figure Salaries",
            font_size=26, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Data points (role, experience, salary)
scatter_data = [
    ("Senior Executive", 17, 127388),
    ("Dev Advocate", 16, 124203),
    ("Manager", 15, 115999),
    ("Dev Experience", 12, 109483),
    ("SRE", 10, 99099),
    ("Cloud Infra. Engineer", 13, 96666),
    ("Blockchain", 9, 85925),
    ("Product Manager", 14, 80000),
    ("Full-stack", 10, 63333),
    ("Front-end", 8, 48787),
    ("Student", 2, 15466),
]

# Plot area
plot_left = MARGIN + Inches(1.0)
plot_top = Inches(1.4)
plot_w = SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN * 2 - Inches(1.5)
plot_h = Inches(5.0)

# Axes lines
axis_color = RgbColor(0x99, 0x99, 0x99)
# Y axis
y_axis = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, plot_left, plot_top, Inches(0.01), plot_h)
y_axis.fill.solid()
y_axis.fill.fore_color.rgb = axis_color
y_axis.line.fill.background()
# X axis
x_axis = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, plot_left, plot_top + plot_h, plot_w, Inches(0.01))
x_axis.fill.solid()
x_axis.fill.fore_color.rgb = axis_color
x_axis.line.fill.background()

max_exp = 18
max_sal = 140000

# Grid lines & labels
for i in range(0, max_sal + 1, 20000):
    y = plot_top + plot_h - (i / max_sal) * plot_h
    tick = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, plot_left - Inches(0.05), y, Inches(0.05), Inches(0.01))
    tick.fill.solid()
    tick.fill.fore_color.rgb = axis_color
    tick.line.fill.background()
    add_textbox(slide, plot_left - Inches(0.9), y - Inches(0.1), Inches(0.8), Inches(0.2),
                f"${i//1000}K", font_size=10, color=axis_color, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)

for i in range(0, max_exp + 1, 2):
    x = plot_left + (i / max_exp) * plot_w
    tick = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, x, plot_top + plot_h, Inches(0.01), Inches(0.05))
    tick.fill.solid()
    tick.fill.fore_color.rgb = axis_color
    tick.line.fill.background()
    add_textbox(slide, x - Inches(0.2), plot_top + plot_h + Inches(0.08), Inches(0.4), Inches(0.2),
                str(i), font_size=10, color=axis_color, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Axis titles
add_textbox(slide, plot_left + plot_w / 2 - Inches(1.0), plot_top + plot_h + Inches(0.35), Inches(2.0), Inches(0.3),
            "Avg. Years of Experience", font_size=12, bold=True, color=TEXT_DARK, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
add_textbox(slide, plot_left - Inches(1.3), plot_top - Inches(0.35), Inches(1.2), Inches(0.3),
            "Median Salary (USD)", font_size=12, bold=True, color=TEXT_DARK, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Data points
for role, exp, sal in scatter_data:
    x = plot_left + (exp / max_exp) * plot_w
    y = plot_top + plot_h - (sal / max_sal) * plot_h
    dot = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, x - Inches(0.06), y - Inches(0.06), Inches(0.12), Inches(0.12))
    dot.fill.solid()
    dot.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_BLUE
    dot.line.color.rgb = WHITE
    dot.line.width = Pt(1.5)
    # label for a few key points
    if role in ("Senior Executive", "Dev Advocate", "Manager", "Student", "Front-end"):
        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.1), y - Inches(0.18), Inches(1.4), Inches(0.2),
                    role, font_size=9, color=TEXT_DARK, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
